refutations.detail: 200 reassignments; share with an effect at least as large: 0.01 (pass)

interpretations.answer: The analysis estimates that New Jersey's 1992 minimum wage rise increased fast food employment by 2.75 employees per restaurant [estimate:1_vs_0.value]. This effect is statistically significant, with a 95% confidence interval ranging from 0.1198 to 5.38 employees [estimate:1_vs_0.ci].
caveats: The design relies on the assumption that, without the minimum wage change, employment trends in New Jersey and Pennsylvania fast food restaurants would have been parallel [design.assumption].
The parallel-trends assumption could not be tested due to the presence of only one pre-period [check:1_vs_0.parallel_untestable].

A placebo test, reassigning treatment, passed [placebo:1_vs_0.placebo_group.passed], showing a new effect of -0.011490226537217136 with a p-value of 0.01 [placebo:1_vs_0.placebo_group.new_effect, placebo:1_vs_0.placebo_group.p_value].
